chunks: A number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:

I wrote to the Imam (peace be upon him) asking him about the Fitra and how much should be paid. He wrote back: 'Six Ratls of dates by the Medinite measure, and that is nine Ratls by the Baghdadi measure.'

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: Ratls, a traditional unit of weight/measurement
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.بِالْبَغْدَادِيِّ: By the Baghdadi (measure), referring to the standard of Baghdad
key_terms.بِالْمَدَنِيِّ: By the Medinite (measure), referring to the standard of Medina
key_terms.تَمْرٍ: Dates, the fruit specified for this charity

ai.seo_question: How much Zakat al-Fitr should be paid in dates according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific quantity of Zakat al-Fitr as six Ratls of dates, highlighting the scholarly practice of adjusting measurements based on regional standards (Medinite vs. Baghdadi). It underscores the practical application of fiqh in ensuring the charity meets the minimum threshold for the poor, reflecting the Imams' attention to economic realities in 9th-century Iraq.
